findings.text: The first paragraph does its job. A newcomer learns what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves before any jargon appears.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The second section on the page is an error message. It was meant to prove Athena's main promise: a commit traced to the models, cost and verdict. A newcomer sees a failure in its place, which weakens the 'why it matters' case.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: This is Athena's homepage, but nearly all of it is a study of firstmate, another tool. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena has to get through states, transitions, a glossary and 45 claims about firstmate. What Athena itself does is shown only indirectly.
findings.source: Title: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: This link appears at the top for every visitor but is meant for the owner. A newcomer has no context for it and may wonder whether it is meant for them.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The next steps are concrete: prerequisites, the clone command, the install script and a one-line first command. A newcomer knows exactly what to do next, and the header links straight to this section.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm ... ./setup.sh ... athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: Several glossary entries say mainly that a term is undefined. That is honest, but a newcomer is left with words they still cannot understand.
findings.source: Glossary entries such as "The firstmate source does not define a durable record." and "The firstmate source does not define a heartbeat."

findings.text: The study cards are carefully hedged but hard to read for someone new. A merge that leaves the state unchanged, plus caveats in brackets, takes several readings to follow.
findings.source: t10 card: "ready → ready ... With yolo on, firstmate merges green work that is in scope (the instructions do not say what qualifies) itself ..."

findings.text: These sections use Athena's internal terms, such as 'recorded boundary' and the studies/ folder, without explaining them. They mean little to someone visiting for the first time.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f1: "The job gave no recorded boundary for running firstmate, so no failure or retry edge was observed"; About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/"

findings.text: Every statement links to exact lines in firstmate's source at a fixed commit. This shows Athena's traceability claim in practice, which is the strongest evidence a newcomer gets on the page.
findings.source: Header: "Each statement below ends with the id of the claim that supports it; the claims, with links to their sources, are listed at the end."
